name: Question 4
problem:
Consider the differential equation 

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}={cos}^{2}⁡(2x-y+1).
$$

Using a substitution of the form $z=2x-y,$ transform the differential equation into an equation of the form ${z}^{′}(x)=f(z).$ What is the function $f(z)?$

html:
Question 4
?

Consider the differential equation dydx=cos2⁡(2x−y+1). Using a substitution of the form z=2x−y, transform the differential equation into an equation of the form z′(x)=f(z). What is the function f(z)?

a
2−cos2⁡(z+1)
b
2−cos2⁡z
c
2cos2⁡(z+1)
d
cos2⁡(2z+1)
e
1+cos2⁡(2z)
Submit
